info.title: INIO Rest API
info.description:
## Overview
The most efficient way to enhance customer loyalty and payment resolution is to integrate our
[RESTFul API](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer).
It allows you to manage customers, create invoices, as well as process payments and create your own customizable invoice templates.
SMS and email communication are also part of the package.
Inio API is organized around [REST](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer).

Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts [form-encoded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POST_(HTTP)#Use_for_submitting_web_forms) request bodies,
returns [JSON-encoded](https://www.json.org/json-en.html) responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.
You can use the Inio API in test mode, which doesn’t affect your live data or interact with the banking networks.

The API key you use to authenticate the request determines whether the request is live mode or test mode.

**The Inio API does support bulk updates. You can work on more than one object per request.**

Log in to see docs with your test key and data.

## Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
This API features Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) implemented in compliance with W3C spec.
And that allows cross-domain communication from the browser.
All responses have a wildcard same-origin which makes them completely public and accessible to everyone, including any code on any site.

## Pagination, Filtering, and Sorting

To enhance the flexibility and control over the data returned by the API, we provide support for pagination, filtering, and sorting.

### Pagination

Pagination allows you to retrieve a subset of the data by specifying the number of records to be returned per page and the page number. The `page` parameter represents the page number, while the `limit` parameter determines the number of records per page. These two parameters are bound together, meaning that the `limit` value determines the maximum number of records that can be returned on a single page.

### Filtering

Filtering enables you to narrow down the results based on specific criteria. You can use the `order` parameter to specify the order in which the results should be sorted. Additionally, you can use any of the fields of the returned items as parameter to filter the results based on specific field values.

### Sorting

Sorting allows you to arrange the results in a specific order. You can use the `sort` parameter to specify the field by which the results should be sorted.

By utilizing pagination, filtering, and sorting, you can efficiently retrieve and manipulate the data from our API according to your specific requirements.

For more detailed information and examples on how to use pagination, filtering, and sorting, please refer to our API documentation.

#### Parameters

- `order` (string): Determines the order of the result - ascending or descending
- `limit` (integer): Determines how many items are in one page. E.g. if we have 50 items and limit is set to 5, there will be 10 pages of 5 items each.
- `page` (integer): Determines which page of the result to return. Starts from 1.
- `sort` (string): Name of a field that will be used to sort the results. Default value is id.

The *Customers* section includes endpoints for managing customer-related operations.
Create a B2C customer Method: POST
URL: /customers 
[
  {
    "clientId": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174005",
    "serviceLineName": "B2C",
    "customerName": "John Doe",
    "SSN": "123456789",
    "languageCode": "EN",
    "distributionEmailAddress": "example@test.com",
    "mobilePhoneNo": "+12345678901",
    "customerNo": "B2C_000001",
    "customerType": "C",
    "customerAddress": {
      "countryCode": "US",
      "city": "Ney York",
      "zipCode": "1A 4B",
      "addressLine1": "Street 1"
    }
  }
]
Create a B2B customers Method: POST
URL: /customers 
[
  {
    "clientId": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174005",
    "serviceLineName": "B2B",
    "customerName": "Atlantic Examples Ltd",
    "languageCode": "EN",
    "distributionEmailAddress": "atl.examples@test.com",
    "customerNo": "B2B_000003",
    "customerType": "B",
    "customerAddress": {
      "countryCode": "SE",
      "city": "Stockholm",
      "zipCode": "1A 4B",
      "addressLine1": "Street 12"
    },
    "orgNr": "12345678",
    "vatNo": "SE12345678",
    "glnNumber": "SE1234567801"
  }
]
Update customer Method: PUT
URL: /customers/{customerId} 
{
  "customerName": "Atlantic Examples 3000 Utd.",
  "languageCode": "EN",
  "distributionEmailAddress": "atl.examples3000@test.com",
  "customerType": "B",
  "customerAddress": {
    "countryCode": "SE",
    "city": "Malmo",
    "zipCode": "1334B",
    "addressLine1": "Street 12"
  },
  "orgNr": "ORG-987654",
  "vatNo": "SE5566778899",
  "SSN": "197504019876",
  "glnNumber": "7359999993333"
}
Partial update customer Method: PATCH
URL: /customers/{customerId} 
{
  "customerName": "Atlantic Examples Ltd.",
  "languageCode": "EN",
  "distributionEmailAddress": "atl.examples@test.com"
}
Create a customer pause Method: POST
URL: /customers/{customerId}/pauses 
{
  "scope": "reminders",
  "startAt": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "endAt": "2026-10-15T00:00:00.000Z",
  "reason": "Customer on holiday"
}
Omit `endAt` (or send `null`) for an indefinite pause. `startAt` must be tomorrow UTC or later. A reason is required.
List customer pauses Method: GET
URL: /customers/{customerId}/pauses Optional query: `status=scheduled` (also `active`, `cancelled`, `completed`). Omit `status` to return every pause.
Get a customer pause Method: GET
URL: /customers/{customerId}/pauses/{pauseId}
Update a customer pause Method: PATCH
URL: /customers/{customerId}/pauses/{pauseId} 
{
  "endAt": "2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z",
  "reason": "Holiday extended"
}
Scope and start date can only change while the pause is still scheduled; an active pause can change only its end date. A reason is required.
Cancel a customer pause Method: POST
URL: /customers/{customerId}/pauses/{pauseId}/cancel 
{
  "reason": "Customer asked to resume"
}
Cancellation takes effect immediately. A reason is required.

subjectMatter.description: Logical or business category of the invoice item. This value is displayed in the invoice PDF and can be used for internal grouping, analytics, or integration with reporting systems.

name.description: Human-readable label of the product or service being invoiced. Shown directly on the invoice. It should clearly describe the item as customers see it (e.g., "Consulting Services", "License Fee").

calcInput.description:

quantity.description: The number of units being billed. It can be fractional, for example 1.5 hours. Together with `unitPrice` it gives the total of the item. The number of decimal places is limited by the calculation strategy of the service line.

get.description:
Retrieve a specific invoice by its invoice number, scoped to the requesting client.

Invoice numbers containing `/` are not supported by this endpoint — for example `INV/205`. Percent-encoding does not help, and such requests fail with a generic 404 instead of the standard error body. `GET /invoices?invoiceNo=INV%2F205` is not subject to this restriction.

Matching is case-sensitive, and leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. All other characters are supported, including spaces and non-ASCII — for example `Crédit 0602` — percent-encoded as usual.

Invoice numbers are unique only within a client, so a number belonging to another client is not returned.

post.summary: Reset the stage of an invoice back to Invoiced or Reminded.
post.description:
Resets an invoice from Reminded or Debt Collection back to Invoiced, or from Debt Collection back to Reminded, with the same business rules as in the back office.

- `targetStage` `invoiced` requires a `dueDate` after today. `reminded` does not accept one: it is calculated.
- `reason` is mandatory. `redistribute` sends the invoice or reminder again; it is forced when `modifyInvoice` changes fields.
- The reset is committed before the response; the escalation restart, fee waiver, document and redistribution run asynchronously. `workflowId` in the response tracks them.
- The action is recorded under the API client name the gateway sets from the access token; without it, `userRealName` or `System`.

Invalid request fields return 400 with `fieldErrors` (`fieldName`, `errorCode`, `message`), e.g. a missing `reason`, a missing `dueDate` for `invoiced`, or a `dueDate` sent for `reminded`.

Business-rule rejections return 400 with one of these codes in `i18nKey`:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_credit_invoice` | Credit invoices cannot be reset. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_debt_collection_closed_or_paid` | The invoice is in debt collection and is paid, closed or cancelled. Its stage cannot be reset. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_reverse_payment_first` | The invoice is paid, closed or cancelled. Reverse the payment in order to allow the reset. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_invalid_transition` | The invoice cannot be reset from its current stage to the target stage. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_due_date_invalid` | The due date is not a valid date. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_due_date_is_today` | The due date must be after today. |
| `errors.invoices.update_due_date_in_past` | The due date is in the past. |
| `errors.invoices.update_due_date_not_after_current_due_date` | The due date must be changed. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_modify_requires_redistribute` | Redistribute is required when invoice details are modified. |
| `errors.invoices.reset_stage_missing_workflows_settings` | The invoice has no escalation settings to plan a restart from. |
